input.question: What makes banks special enough to be able to hold electronic money? What is stopping people from just opening their own accounts?
input.ground_truth: Banks are tightly regulated by the government, required to follow thousands of laws and rules, and subject to constant inspection and detailed audits at any time. Therefore they are trusted to manage certain financial tasks.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What makes banks special enough to be able to hold electronic money? What is stopping people from just opening their own accounts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big toy box at home where you keep all your toys safe. Now, imagine if everyone in your class wanted to keep their toys safe too, but they didn’t want to carry them everywhere. So, you and your friends decide to have one super-special toy box at school, and you all trust the teacher to look after it.

Banks are like that super-special toy box, but for money. They keep everyone’s money safe in a special computer (that’s what “electronic money” means!). The bank is trusted by everyone because it follows special rules to make sure no one steals your money. 

Now, if you just made your own “bank” in your room, no one would trust it. Your friends might think, “What if you lose my money? What if you forget how much I have?” So, banks have to be special—they have to follow rules, show they are honest, and prove they can keep everyone’s money safe.

That’s why you can’t just open your own bank. You have to be really, really careful and follow lots of rules to make sure everyone’s money is safe.
